title: PHARM · Bupropion XL: do not crush (XL MEANS WHOLE) (high stakes, night shift, Smart Prep errors)
hook: Nurses: she can't swallow pills. Crush the XL?
hook_backups: Nurses: crushed into applesauce at 5 AM. Then a seizure.
Nurses: two letters on the label decide everything. Which?
belief: Any pill can be crushed if the patient can't swallow it.

save_card.title: DO NOT CRUSH (XL MEANS WHOLE)

caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 5:20 AM med pass. She's 73, trouble swallowing since a stroke. Bupropion XL (extended release) 300 mg every morning.

❌ 3 mistakes, 3 error types
1️⃣ Missed keyword: crushed every pill, never read "XL"
2️⃣ Scope error: handed the cup to the nursing assistant to give
3️⃣ Acted too late: twitching and jitters called "just anxious"
➡️ 6:30 AM: a seizure. Rapid response.

💊 Bupropion XL (XL MEANS WHOLE)
• XL tablets release the dose slowly over the day
• Crushed, the whole day's dose hits at once
• Bupropion's seizure risk climbs with dose and speed

✅ The right move
• XL, ER (extended release), SR (sustained release), CR (controlled release), LA (long acting) on the label: never crush. A few can be split or opened: ask pharmacy
• Can't swallow it? Hold it and call pharmacy and the provider for another form
• In the hospital, the nurse gives the meds
• New twitching or jitters: check her, seizure precautions, report

🧠 XL means whole. Never crush.

rn_checks: Bupropion XL must be swallowed whole; crushing raises the risk of adverse effects including seizures (label)
Story: crushed 300 mg XL at 5:22, jitters and twitching by 6:05, seizure 6:30. Realistic timing?
Hospital wording: 'In the hospital, the nurse gives the meds' (certified medication aides give meds in some long-term care settings)
Extended-release forms: never crush; a few can be split or opened (for example some ER tablets and capsules), so 'ask pharmacy'. Bupropion XL itself: swallow whole (label). OK?
Memory phrase is NEW: (XL MEANS WHOLE). Keep or swap?
Story clock is the 5 to 6 AM med pass (bupropion XL is a morning dose). OK for the night-shift rule?
Smart Prep labels: MISSED KEYWORD, SCOPE ERROR, ACTED TOO LATE. Fit?
Choice answer B; keyword PHARM; hook, cover and caption line 1 open with 'Nurses:'
Severe stroke is a listed predisposing factor for bupropion seizures (label), which fits this patient
